name: Kalmanatas
backstory: One of the professors of the University of Tyrnea, recently reopened after the town's revival brought about by Folkorlo's glass factory. Professor of concrete and bricks, teaching construction — the mixture of elements to create durable "aggregate stoning," as he insists on calling it, rather proud of the pun.

criterion.standard: counts a life well spent only if what he built in Tyrnea is still standing after he's gone
criterion.wasted_life: one spent building things that don't outlast the person who paid for them
criterion.trusts: a wall you can put your hand on, not a rumor about one
criterion.distrusts: a claim about a structure nobody's actually tested

routines.routine_actions: lectures on binding ratios and load-bearing walls, chalks diagrams of aggregate mixes on the board, argues with students who think faster-drying means better
walks the quarry face with the cutters most mornings, sorting stone by grade before it ever reaches the kiln or the mixing yard
holds court most evenings on why his mix outlasts the old mortar, buys a round when someone finally admits he's right

arc.premise: Kalmanatas wants to prove his aggregate-stone method by using it to shore up the university's own crumbling east wing before the next class term - the same technique he lectures on, tested where anyone can see it fail or hold. Resolution: the wing holds through a full term's use, or it doesn't - a crack reopens, a beam gives, and the technique gets quietly dropped from the syllabus.
